lead: Knock, acceleration, torque and angular-rate sensors turn mechanical vibration and motion into electrical signals. The engine ECU uses a knock sensor to hear detonation and retard spark before damage. Airbag and ESP systems use accelerometers and gyroscopes to detect a crash or a skid. Torque sensors measure shaft twist; LIDAR measures distance by light time of flight; flex-fuel sensors measure ethanol content. These sensors protect the engine and stabilise the vehicle, so they sit in both engine control and safety systems.
prereq: You need: 3.1 Sensor basics and signal conditioning; 3.4 Hall and optical position sensing; basic mechanics.

blocks.text: Knock is uncontrolled detonation after the spark. It hits the engine block at a frequency set by the combustion chamber, usually in the 5–15 kHz band. A piezoelectric knock sensor bolts to the block. Its crystal makes charge when the block vibrates. Charge sensitivity d is often given in pC/N. A charge amplifier converts this charge to a voltage. A band-pass filter then keeps only the knock band. A rectifier makes an envelope. The ECU opens a window from the crank-angle signal around top dead centre and compares the envelope with a threshold. Above threshold, it retards spark angle. The window stops the ECU reacting to valve or injector noise at other crank angles.
q = d F,   V = q / C<sub>f</sub>
blocks.where: q is charge (C); d is charge sensitivity (C/N); F is knock force (N); V is output voltage (V); C<sub>f</sub> is feedback capacitance (F).

blocks.text: A MEMS accelerometer has a proof mass on silicon springs. Comb fingers on the mass form capacitors with fixed fingers. Acceleration moves the mass, so one capacitance rises and the other falls. The circuit reads the differential capacitance, which is proportional to acceleration. A high-g accelerometer in the airbag system detects a crash pulse. A low-g lateral accelerometer in ESP measures cornering. Some syllabi call the lateral accelerometer and yaw-rate gyro the ESP sensors. A MEMS gyroscope vibrates a proof mass and uses the Coriolis force to measure angular rate. The output is rate in °/s, not angle. The ECU can integrate rate to get angle, but bias and noise make the angle drift. Vehicle stability algorithms combine rate, lateral acceleration, wheel speeds and steering angle. See Unit 5, Electronic stability program (ESP), for the control law.

Torque sensors measure twist in a shaft. A strain-gauge bridge bonded to the shaft changes resistance with shear strain. A magnetoelastic shaft changes magnetic permeability when twisted; a coil reads the change. A surface-acoustic-wave (SAW) torque sensor uses a wave delay that changes with strain. These sensors help transmission control and electric power steering. A strain-gauge torque sensor on a steering column helps electric power steering apply assist in proportion to driver torque. LIDAR measures distance by time of flight. A light pulse leaves the sensor, reflects from an object and returns. The round-trip distance is c t, so d = c t / 2. Here d is distance (m), c is speed of light (3×10⁸ m/s), and t is round-trip time (s). A flex-fuel sensor estimates ethanol in petrol. Ethanol has a higher dielectric constant than petrol, so a capacitive sensor changes with fuel composition. The ECU then adjusts fuel quantity and spark timing. Detailed ADAS and LIDAR use are in Unit 5.

examples.question: A piezoelectric knock sensor has charge sensitivity d = 2 pC/N. A knock force of 50 N acts on it. The charge amplifier has feedback capacitor C<sub>f</sub> = 1000 pF. Find the charge produced and the output voltage.
examples.answer: The charge is 100 pC and the charge-amplifier output is 0.10 V.
examples.check:
d = 2e-12
F = 50.0
q = d * F
Cf = 1000e-12
V = q / Cf
print(q * 1e12)
print(V)

traps: Do not amplify all engine noise: knock detection uses a band-pass filter around the knock frequency and a crank-angle window.
A gyroscope measures angular rate, not angle; integrating rate drifts because of bias and noise.
Piezo charge sensitivity is in pC/N, not V/g. A charge amplifier gain is set by C<sub>f</sub>; cable capacitance matters little.
LIDAR time of flight is round trip: divide c t by 2. Mixing ns and s gives a factor of 10⁹ error.
A torque sensor measures shaft torque, not engine brake torque; mounting and shaft material affect sensitivity.

quiz.q: What physical quantity does a knock sensor measure, and what does the ECU do with it?
quiz.a: It measures structure-borne vibration in the engine block in the knock band. The ECU retards spark angle to stop detonation.

quiz.q: Why is a band-pass filter used in the knock channel instead of a wideband amplifier?
quiz.a: Engine noise covers many frequencies. The 5–15 kHz band contains knock energy and rejects valve and injector noise. A crank-angle window further limits listening to the firing event.

quiz.q: A piezo knock sensor has d = 5 pC/N. A knock force is 40 N. Feedback capacitor C<sub>f</sub> = 2000 pF. Find charge and output voltage.
A yaw-rate gyro outputs 30 °/s for 2 s. The ECU integrates it and gets 60°, but the true angle is 55°. Give two reasons and one fix.
quiz.a: Bias offset and noise integrate into drift; temperature changes bias. Fix: zero the gyro when the vehicle is stationary and fuse with steering angle or accelerometer.

quiz.q: What does a MEMS capacitive accelerometer use as its moving part?
quiz.a: A proof mass with comb fingers that changes differential capacitance when accelerated.

quiz.q: Why does a piezoelectric knock sensor need a charge amplifier rather than a simple voltage amplifier?
quiz.a: The piezo source has very high output impedance and cable capacitance shunts charge. A charge amplifier holds the input near virtual ground and sets gain by C<sub>f</sub>, so cable capacitance has little effect.

quiz.q: A LIDAR pulse returns after 200 ns. Take c = 3×10⁸ m/s. Find the distance.
quiz.a: Round trip: 2d = c t = 3×10⁸ × 200×10⁻⁹ = 60 m. d = 30 m.

beyond: Not for the exam. Automotive MEMS now combine a 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyro in one inertial measurement unit for ESP and ADAS. Piezoelectric MEMS and thin-film sensors are replacing some bulk ceramics. Magnetoelastic and SAW torque sensors are used in electric power steering and driveline test benches. Researchers are working on optical and chip-scale LIDAR for ADAS. Search terms: MEMS comb accelerometer, Coriolis vibratory gyroscope, magnetoelastic torque sensor, SAW torque sensor, flex-fuel dielectric sensor, automotive LiDAR time of flight.
